This research sits on the three edges of one triad — **Human**, **Environment**, and **Information** — asking how people, environmental risk, and the information space shape each other.

## 01 Human × Environment

**Research question:** how do human behavior and environmental risk interact in space and time?

::: {#projects-he}
:::

## 02 Environment × Information

**Research question:** how are nature and biodiversity perceived and represented in the information space?

::: {#projects-ei}
:::

## 03 Human × Information

**Research question:** how is knowledge structured across languages, platforms, and networks?

::: {#projects-hi}
:::

## Funding

Active competitive grants supporting this research.

**Language Disparities in Biodiversity Knowledge: Quantifying and Explaining Cultural Bias Using Multilingual Wikipedia and Large Language Models** — JSPS KAKENHI Grant-in-Aid for Scientific Research (C), [26K09459](https://kaken.nii.ac.jp/en/grant/KAKENHI-PROJECT-26K09459/), FY2026–2028, Principal Investigator. Quantifies biodiversity knowledge disparities across languages and cultural spheres for roughly 2,000 threatened species, using Wikipedia in 11 languages and large language models. Drives the [Language Gaps in Biodiversity Knowledge](biodiversity-language-gap/index.qmd) project.
